rig.scrubTiming: The daemon log carries no timestamps and the tmux children live ~10 ms each (a 20 ms pgrep sampler never caught one), so the cost was measured through the real TmuxRuntime.scrubServerEnvironment with a sequential Bun.spawn runner (the daemon's runner is sequential too) on scratch servers at this box's current load (load average 106–110): 150 planted STALE_VAR_* + a 5-line PEM + an attach (161 global non-marker lines, 3 session entries) → removed=154, 313 tmux calls (1 dump -g + 154 probes + 154 -u + 1 set-option + 1 dump -t + 3 session probes/-u), 3700 ms wall = 11.8 ms per tmux call; 5 planted + PEM + attach → removed=9, 23 calls, 296 ms = 12.9 ms/call. The scrub is 2 tmux calls per disallowed candidate (probe + unset) plus one per fragment candidate (probe only) plus 3 fixed; production's 60–140 candidates ⇒ ~125–285 calls ⇒ ~1.5–3.5 s at this load, proportionally less when the box is idle. On the rig itself the whole boot from daemon start (12:21:30) to the first pane (12:21:45) was 15 s, dominated by the two OMP probes; the 137-name scrub is inside that window. Phase A's 137 removals therefore cost roughly 137×2+~10 ≈ 285 tmux calls ≈ 3 s.
